claim: Klf5 mRNA expression in regenerating TA muscles was upregulated 2 and 4 days after cardiotoxin-induced injury compared to intact muscle.
source: As compared to expression in intact (uninjured) muscle, expression of Klf5 mRNA in regenerating TA muscles was upregulated 2 and 4 days after injury, as was expression of myogenic factors (Pax7, Myod1, Myog and Myh3) (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 1A comparing intact and regenerating muscle at different time points after CTX injection.

claim: Pax7, Myod1, Myog and Myh3 mRNA expression in regenerating TA muscles was upregulated 2 and 4 days after cardiotoxin-induced injury compared to intact muscle.
source: As compared to expression in intact (uninjured) muscle, expression of Klf5 mRNA in regenerating TA muscles was upregulated 2 and 4 days after injury, as was expression of myogenic factors (Pax7, Myod1, Myog and Myh3) (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 1A comparing intact and regenerating muscle at different time points after CTX injection.

claim: Little or no Klf5 is expressed in Pax7-positive quiescent satellite cells in intact muscle.
source: Our immunohistochemistry results showed that little or no Klf5 is expressed in Pax7-positive, quiescent SCs or myonuclei that constitute intact muscle (Figure 1B upper panel, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Klf5 expression remained very low in Pax7-positive activated satellite cells 7 days after CTX-induced muscle injury.
source: At that time, expression of Klf5 remained very low in Pax7-positive, activated SCs (Figure 1B, middle panel, arrows).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 1B middle panel.

claim: Higher levels of Klf5 were detected in differentiating myocytes expressing myogenin 7 days after CTX injury.
source: However, higher levels of Klf5 were detected in differentiating myocytes, which expressed myogenin 7 days after injury (Figure 1B, lower panel, arrowheads).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 1B lower panel.

claim: Klf5 was detected within the centrally located nuclei of regenerating myofibers.
source: Klf5 was also detected within the centrally located nuclei of regenerating myofibers.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and is supported by immunohistochemistry observations.

claim: Klf5 is markedly upregulated in differentiating myocytes and regenerating myofibers during the course of muscle regeneration in vivo.
source: These results indicate that Klf5 is markedly upregulated in differentiating myocytes and regenerating myofibers during the course of muscle regeneration in vivo.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the immunohistochemistry data presented in Figure 1B.

claim: After the first passage, nearly 100% of satellite cells isolated from EDL muscle were MyoD positive.
source: After the first passage, nearly 100% of cells were MyoD positive, confirming the high purity of the muscle cell cultures (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B,C.

claim: Over 70% of purified satellite cells were positive for Pax7.
source: Over 70% of the purified cells were also positive for Pax7 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Little or no Klf5 was detected in a fraction of activated satellite cells expressing Pax7 and MyoD in culture.
source: Consistent with the in vivo results, little or no Klf5 was detected in a fraction of the activated SCs expressing Pax7 and MyoD (Figure 1C, upper panel).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 1C upper panel.

claim: Approximately 75% of Pax7-positive cells were weakly positive for Klf5.
source: Approximately 75% of Pax7-positive cells were also weakly positive for Klf5 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Klf5 was induced in differentiating myoblasts exhibiting an absence or low Pax7 expression.
source: Klf5 was induced in differentiating myoblasts exhibiting an absence or low Pax7 expression (Figure 1C, arrows, Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1D.

claim: After differentiation for 2 days, Klf5 was strongly expressed in the nuclei of differentiating myotubes and co-localized with myogenin.
source: After differentiation for 2 days, Klf5 was strongly expressed in the nuclei of differentiating myotubes and co-localized with myogenin (Figure 1C, middle panel, Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 1C middle panel and Figure 1—figure supplement 1E.

claim: By day 4 of differentiation, strong Klf5 expression was undetectable in the nuclei of larger, fused myotubes that had also lost myogenin expression.
source: However, the strong Klf5 expression was transient, and by day 4 of differentiation it was undetectable in the nuclei of larger, fused myotubes that had also lost myogenin expression (Figure 1C, arrowheads).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Klf5 is induced in differentiating myoblasts during muscle differentiation and then downregulated in mature myotubes.
source: These in vitro observations indicate that Klf5 is induced in differentiating myoblasts during muscle differentiation and then downregulated in mature myotubes.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the immunostaining data presented in Figure 1C.

claim: Pax7CE/+ mice can ablate almost 100% of satellite cells when crossed with R26RGFP-DTA/+ mice.
source: The Pax7CE/+ mice were previously shown to be able to ablate almost 100% of SCs when crossed with R26RGFP-DTA/+mice (Lepper et al., 2009, 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies by Lepper et al.

claim: Pax7CE/+;Klf5flox/flox mice or control Pax7+/+;Klf5flox/flox mice displayed no obvious phenotypic alterations under physiological conditions 28 days after tamoxifen treatment.
source: Muscle histology revealed that Pax7CE/+;Klf5flox/flox mice or control Pax7+/+;Klf5flox/flox mice displayed no obvious phenotypic alterations under physiological conditions and exhibited no morphological alterations in their skeletal muscle stained with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) 28 days after tamoxifen treatment (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by H&E staining data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: On day 4 after CTX injury, mRNA expression of Myog and Myh3 was significantly lower in regenerating muscles from Pax7CE/+;Klf5flox/flox mice than control mice.
source: On day 4 after injury, mRNA expression of Myog and Myh3 was significantly lower in regenerating muscles from Pax7CE/+;Klf5flox/flox mice than control mice; Pax7 and Myod1 levels also tended to be reduced, but the differences did not reach statistical significance (Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: On day 4 after CTX injury, Pax7 and Myod1 mRNA levels tended to be reduced in regenerating muscles from Pax7CE/+;Klf5flox/flox mice compared to control mice, but the differences did not reach statistical significance.
source: On day 4 after injury, mRNA expression of Myog and Myh3 was significantly lower in regenerating muscles from Pax7CE/+;Klf5flox/flox mice than control mice; Pax7 and Myod1 levels also tended to be reduced, but the differences did not reach statistical significance (Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: On day 7 after CTX injury, control mice revealed efficient muscle regeneration characterized by regenerated myofibers with decreased expression of eMyHC.
source: On day 7 after injury, H&E and immunofluorescent staining in control mice revealed efficient muscle regeneration characterized by regenerated myofibers with decreased expression of eMyHC, a marker of immature myofibers (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by H&E and immunofluorescent staining data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The regeneration process was significantly impaired in Pax7CE/+;Klf5flox/flox mice on day 7 after CTX injury.
source: On the contrary, the regeneration process was significantly impaired in Pax7CE/+;Klf5flox/flox mice.
evidence: The claim is supported by histological data shown in Figure 2B-D.

claim: Pax7CE/+;Klf5flox/flox mice exhibited necrotic fibers and infiltrating inflammatory cells on day 7 after CTX injury.
source: These mice exhibited necrotic fibers and infiltrating inflammatory cells, and an extensive area of regenerating myofibers with prolonged expression of eMyHC (Figure 2B and C).
evidence: The claim is supported by histological data shown in Figure 2B and C.

claim: Pax7CE/+;Klf5flox/flox mice exhibited an extensive area of regenerating myofibers with prolonged expression of eMyHC on day 7 after CTX injury.
source: These mice exhibited necrotic fibers and infiltrating inflammatory cells, and an extensive area of regenerating myofibers with prolonged expression of eMyHC (Figure 2B and C).
evidence: The claim is supported by histological data shown in Figure 2B and C.

claim: Klf5 deletion in satellite cells significantly shifted regenerating myofibers towards smaller diameters on day 7 after CTX injury.
source: Analysis of the distribution of myofiber diameters revealed that Klf5 deletion in SCs significantly shifted regenerating myofibers towards smaller diameters (Figure 2D), suggesting differentiation and/or maturation of muscle fibers were impaired by the loss of Klf5.
evidence: The claim is supported by myofiber diameter distribution data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Differentiation and/or maturation of muscle fibers were impaired by the loss of Klf5.
source: Analysis of the distribution of myofiber diameters revealed that Klf5 deletion in SCs significantly shifted regenerating myofibers towards smaller diameters (Figure 2D), suggesting differentiation and/or maturation of muscle fibers were impaired by the loss of Klf5.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the myofiber diameter data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Twenty-eight days after CTX injury in control mice, muscle regeneration was nearly complete, as evidenced by the presence of regenerated, mature fibers and disappearance of inflammatory cells.
source: Twenty-eight days after CTX injury in control mice, muscle regeneration was nearly complete, as evidenced by the presence of regenerated, mature fibers and disappearance of inflammatory cells, as previous described (Ingalls et al., 1998).
evidence: The claim is supported by histological observations and a citation to Ingalls et al., 1998.

claim: The regeneration process was retarded in the injured muscle of Pax7CE/+;Klf5flox/flox mice 28 days after CTX injury.
source: However, the regeneration process was retarded in the injured muscle of Pax7CE/+;Klf5flox/flox mice, and massive deposition of collagen I, indicating enhanced fibrosis, was observed (Figure 2E).
evidence: The claim is supported by histological data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Massive deposition of collagen I, indicating enhanced fibrosis, was observed in Pax7CE/+;Klf5flox/flox mice 28 days after CTX injury.
source: However, the regeneration process was retarded in the injured muscle of Pax7CE/+;Klf5flox/flox mice, and massive deposition of collagen I, indicating enhanced fibrosis, was observed (Figure 2E).
evidence: The claim is supported by collagen I staining data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: The regenerating myofibers were still shifted toward smaller diameters in Pax7CE/+;Klf5flox/flox mice 28 days after CTX injury.
source: In addition, the regenerating myofibers were still shifted toward smaller diameters (Figure 2F).
evidence: The claim is supported by myofiber diameter distribution data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Klf5 is required for proper satellite cell-mediated muscle regeneration after skeletal muscle injury.
source: These results indicate that Klf5 is required for proper SC-mediated muscle regeneration after skeletal muscle injury.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the muscle regeneration data presented in Figure 2.

claim: Klf5 mRNA was induced after induction of C2C12 cells differentiation and reached a peak on day 4 of myoblast differentiation.
source: Klf5 mRNA was induced after induction of C2C12 cells differentiation and reached a peak on day 4 of myoblast differentiation (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Klf5 protein was detected after 2 days of C2C12 differentiation.
source: Klf5 protein was detected after 2 days of differentiation (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B) and was frequently colocalized with myogenin in the nuclei of differentiating myotubes, which is consistent with the pattern observed during myogenic differentiation of SCs (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B and Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Klf5 protein was frequently colocalized with myogenin in the nuclei of differentiating C2C12 myotubes.
source: Klf5 protein was detected after 2 days of differentiation (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B) and was frequently colocalized with myogenin in the nuclei of differentiating myotubes, which is consistent with the pattern observed during myogenic differentiation of SCs (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B and Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B and Figure 1C.

claim: Klf5 protein was not detectable after induction of differentiation in any of the three Klf5-null C2C12 clones.
source: Klf5 protein was not detectable after induction of differentiation in any of the three Klf5-null clones (Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 2A), and myotube formation was significantly impaired as compared to the control clones (Figure 3 and Figure 3—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Myotube formation was significantly impaired in Klf5-null C2C12 clones as compared to the control clones.
source: Klf5 protein was not detectable after induction of differentiation in any of the three Klf5-null clones (Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 2A), and myotube formation was significantly impaired as compared to the control clones (Figure 3 and Figure 3—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 3 and Figure 3—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Impaired myotube formation in Klf5-null C2C12 clones occurred concomitantly with decreased expression of myogenin and MyHC on day 4 of differentiation.
source: This effect occurred concomitantly with decreased expression of myogenin and MyHC on day 4 of differentiation (Figure 3A–C).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining and Western blot data shown in Figure 3A–C.

claim: Klf5-null C2C12 cells transfected with RV-Klf5 successfully formed myotubes when stimulated to differentiate.
source: Klf5-null C2C12 cells transfected with RV-Klf5 successfully formed myotubes when stimulated to differentiate, whereas Klf5-null cells infected with an empty retrovirus failed to do so (Figure 3D).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Klf5-null C2C12 cells infected with an empty retrovirus failed to form myotubes when stimulated to differentiate.
source: Klf5-null C2C12 cells transfected with RV-Klf5 successfully formed myotubes when stimulated to differentiate, whereas Klf5-null cells infected with an empty retrovirus failed to do so (Figure 3D).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Expression of MyHC and myogenin was partially rescued by the forced expression of Klf5 in Klf5-null C2C12 cells.
source: In addition, immunohistochemistry and western blotting demonstrated that expression of MyHC and myogenin was partially rescued by the forced expression of Klf5 (Figure 3D–F).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining and Western blot data shown in Figure 3D–F.

claim: Klf5 is required for myoblast differentiation.
source: Klf5 thus appears to be required for a myoblast differentiation.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the rescue experiment data presented in Figure 3.

claim: Klf5 knockdown efficiently inhibited the induction of myogenin in C2C12 cells.
source: Immunohistochemistry indicated that the Klf5 knockdown efficiently inhibited the induction of myogenin (Figure 3—figure supplement 3A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3A and B.

claim: Myotube formation was significantly impaired in Klf5 knockdown C2C12 cells.
source: At the same time, myotube formation was significantly impaired in the Klf5 knockdown cells, as quantified based on the Fusion index, which represents the fraction of MyHC-positive, fused myotubes that contain at least three nuclei (Figure 3—figure supplement 3C and D).
evidence: The claim is supported by fusion index data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3C and D.

claim: Klf5 knockdown did not affect C2C12 cell proliferation.
source: Although previous reports have shown the involvement of Klf5 in controlling cell proliferation in several cancer cell lines (Sun et al., 2001), Klf5 knockdown did not affect C2C12 cell proliferation (Figure 3—figure supplement 3E).
evidence: The claim is supported by growth curve data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3E and contrasted with previous reports cited.

claim: Levels of Klf6, Klf13, Klf15, and Klf16 expression were modestly but significantly increased in Klf5 knockdown cells on day 3.
source: Levels of Klf6, Klf13, Klf15, and Klf16 expression were modestly, but significantly, increased in Klf5 knockdown cells on day 3 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Expression of Klf10 and Klf11 was decreased in Klf5 knockdown cells on day 3.
source: On the other hand, expression of Klf10 and Klf11 was decreased in Klf5 knockdown cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Expression of a set of genes involved in myogenesis was significantly decreased in Klf5 knockdown cells.
source: In line with the suppressed myoblast differentiation, expression of a set of genes involved in myogenesis was significantly decreased in Klf5 knockdown cells (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Among the 12,744 expressed transcripts, 1472 with RefSeq annotations were reduced by >1.5-fold on day 3 in the Klf5 knockdown cells as compared to the control cells.
source: Among the 12,744 expressed transcripts (normalized counts >4), 1472 with RefSeq annotations were reduced by >1.5-fold on day 3 in the Klf5 knockdown cells as compared to the control cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq analysis.

claim: Genes whose expression was reduced by Klf5 knockdown had significant enrichment of functional annotations for myogenesis and muscle cell development.
source: Gene ontology analysis revealed that the genes whose expression was reduced by Klf5 knockdown had significant enrichment of functional annotations for myogenesis and muscle cell development (Figure 4B).
evidence: The claim is supported by gene ontology analysis shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Among the 934 genes exhibiting a >1.5-fold increase in expression in Klf5 knockdown cells, no gene sets directly related to myogenesis were significantly enriched as compared to control cells on day 3.
source: Among the 934 genes exhibiting a >1.5-fold increase in expression in Klf5 knockdown cells, no gene sets directly related to myogenesis were significantly enriched as compared to control cells on day 3 (Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by gene ontology analysis.

claim: The effect of Klf5 knockdown on the expression of MyoD-regulated genes became more pronounced as the course of differentiation proceeded.
source: The effect of Klf5 knockdown on the expression of MyoD-regulated genes became more pronounced as the course of differentiation proceeded (Figure 4C), and expression of those MyoD-regulated genes on day 3 was significantly decreased by Klf5 knockdown (Figure 4C and D).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Expression of MyoD-regulated genes on day 3 was significantly decreased by Klf5 knockdown.
source: The effect of Klf5 knockdown on the expression of MyoD-regulated genes became more pronounced as the course of differentiation proceeded (Figure 4C), and expression of those MyoD-regulated genes on day 3 was significantly decreased by Klf5 knockdown (Figure 4C and D).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 4C and D.

claim: Expression of Myog, Mybph, Myl4 and Myom2 was significantly decreased by Klf5 knockdown in C2C12 cells on day 3 post-differentiation.
source: Quantitative PCR analysis confirmed that expression of MyoD-regulated genes, as exemplified by Myog, Mybph, Myl4 and Myom2, was significantly decreased by Klf5 knockdown in C2C12 cells on day 3 post-differentiation (Figure 4F).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: Klf5 is required for expression of MyoD-regulated genes.
source: This indicates that Klf5 is required for expression of these MyoD-regulated genes.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the qPCR data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: The top motifs in the MyoD-bound cistrome included ones closely matched with known consensus myogenin (E-box), Mef2 and Klf5 binding motifs.
source: Remarkably, de novo motif analysis revealed that the top motifs in the MyoD-bound cistrome included ones closely matched with known consensus myogenin (E-box), Mef2 and Klf5 binding motifs, which suggests potential co-localization of MyoD, Mef2 and Klf5 at MyoD-regulated enhancers (Figure 4G).
evidence: The claim is supported by de novo motif analysis shown in Figure 4G.

claim: The presence of myogenin, Mef2 and Klf5 binding motifs in the MyoD-bound cistrome suggests potential co-localization of MyoD, Mef2 and Klf5 at MyoD-regulated enhancers.
source: Remarkably, de novo motif analysis revealed that the top motifs in the MyoD-bound cistrome included ones closely matched with known consensus myogenin (E-box), Mef2 and Klf5 binding motifs, which suggests potential co-localization of MyoD, Mef2 and Klf5 at MyoD-regulated enhancers (Figure 4G).
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the de novo motif analysis shown in Figure 4G.

claim: The Sp1 motif is enriched in the MyoD binding regions.
source: Indeed, enrichment analysis of a known Sp1 motif showed that the Sp1 motif is enriched in the MyoD binding regions (Figure 4G).
evidence: The claim is supported by motif enrichment analysis shown in Figure 4G.

claim: Klf5 bound to the regulatory regions of myogenesis-related genes, as exemplified by Myog, Myod1, Myl4 and Mybph, throughout the course of differentiation.
source: As expected, Klf5 bound to the regulatory regions of myogenesis-related genes, as exemplified by Myog, Myod1, Myl4 and Mybph, throughout the course of differentiation (Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: MyoD and Mef2D binding was frequently observed at myogenesis-related gene loci.
source: MyoD and Mef2D binding was frequently observed at those gene loci.
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Approximately half of the Klf5 peaks on day 5 had significant MyoD binding peaks in close proximity.
source: Approximately half of the Klf5 peaks had significant MyoD binding peaks in close proximity.
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-seq analysis shown in Figure 5B.

claim: An association with Mef2D was observed in many Klf5 binding regions.
source: An association with Mef2D was also observed in many Klf5 binding regions.
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-seq analysis shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Among 4382 Klf5 peaks observed on day 5 post-differentiation, 757 loci (17.2%) were also bound by both MyoD and Mef2D.
source: Among 4382 Klf5 peaks observed on day 5 post-differentiation, 757 loci (17.2%) were also bound by both MyoD and Mef2D, and another 1467 sites (33.4%) were bound by either MyoD or Mef2D (Figure 5E).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-seq analysis shown in Figure 5E.

claim: Among 4382 Klf5 peaks observed on day 5 post-differentiation, 1467 sites (33.4%) were bound by either MyoD or Mef2D.
source: Among 4382 Klf5 peaks observed on day 5 post-differentiation, 757 loci (17.2%) were also bound by both MyoD and Mef2D, and another 1467 sites (33.4%) were bound by either MyoD or Mef2D (Figure 5E).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-seq analysis shown in Figure 5E.

claim: Klf5 binding to the MyoD and Mef2D binding peaks increased as differentiation progressed.
source: Moreover, Klf5 binding to the MyoD and Mef2D binding peaks increased as differentiation progressed (Figure 5C and D, compare day 0 vs. day 2 and 5).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-seq analysis shown in Figure 5C and D.

claim: Klf5 directly associated with MyoD and Mef2 in vitro.
source: Co-immunoprecipitation showed that Klf5 directly associated with MyoD and Mef2 in vitro (Figure 5F).
evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: Klf5, MyoD and Mef2 work together to drive expression of a set of genes involved in myogenic differentiation.
source: These results suggest that Klf5, MyoD and Mef2 work together to drive expression of a set of genes involved in myogenic differentiation.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the ChIP-seq and co-immunoprecipitation data.

claim: A majority of regions that increasingly acquire Klf5 binding during differentiation are also bound by MyoD in proximity to the Klf5 within myotubes.
source: Collectively then, a majority of regions that increasingly acquire Klf5 binding during differentiation are also bound by MyoD in proximity to the Klf5 within myotubes.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 3.

claim: At many observed Klf5 binding regions in myoblasts, binding is decreased during differentiation and not associated with MyoD binding within myotubes.
source: On the other hand, at many observed Klf5 binding regions in myoblasts, binding is decreased during differentiation and not associated with MyoD binding within myotubes.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3.

claim: Klf5 has different targets and functions in myoblasts vs. myotubes.
source: These results suggest that Klf5 has different targets and functions in myoblasts vs. myotubes.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the differential Klf5 binding patterns observed in myoblasts vs. myotubes.

claim: The top motif among the Klf5 cistrome matches the consensus of Krüppel-like factor.
source: Analysis of Klf5-bound motifs revealed that the top motif among the Klf5 cistrome matches the consensus of Krüppel-like factor (Figure 5G).
evidence: The claim is supported by de novo motif analysis shown in Figure 5G.

claim: The Myf5 (E-box consensus bound by MRF, including MyoD) and Mef2D motifs were identified in the de novo motif analysis of Klf5-bound regions.
source: The Myf5 (E-box consensus bound by MRF, including MyoD) and Mef2D motifs were also identified in the de novo motif analysis, suggesting that colocalization of Klf5, MyoD and Mef2 are programmed by cis-regulatory logic.
evidence: The claim is supported by de novo motif analysis shown in Figure 5G.

claim: Colocalization of Klf5, MyoD and Mef2 are programmed by cis-regulatory logic.
source: The Myf5 (E-box consensus bound by MRF, including MyoD) and Mef2D motifs were also identified in the de novo motif analysis, suggesting that colocalization of Klf5, MyoD and Mef2 are programmed by cis-regulatory logic.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the presence of multiple transcription factor motifs in Klf5-bound regions.

claim: Klf5 alone activated the Myog reporter in luciferase assays.
source: We found that Klf5 alone activated the Myog reporter.
evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase assay data shown in Figure 5H.

claim: Klf5, MyoD and Mef2D activated the Myog reporter additively in luciferase assays.
source: Moreover, Klf5, MyoD and Mef2D activated the Myog reporter additively (Figure 5H).
evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase assay data shown in Figure 5H.

claim: Klf5 is an active transcription factor for myogenesis, cooperating with MyoD and Mef2.
source: Together, these findings indicate that Klf5 is an active transcription factor for myogenesis, cooperating with MyoD and Mef2.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the luciferase assay data shown in Figure 5H.

claim: Levels of MyoD and Mef2 protein were not affected by Klf5 deletion.
source: Although levels of MyoD and Mef2 protein were not affected by Klf5 deletion (Figure 6—figure supplement 1), ChIP-seq revealed that MyoD binding was markedly decreased in Klf5 knockout cells compared to the GFP-targeted control cells on 3 day post-differentiation, as exemplified with Myod1, Myog, Myl4 and Mybph (Figure 6A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: MyoD binding was markedly decreased in Klf5 knockout cells compared to the GFP-targeted control cells on day 3 post-differentiation.
source: Although levels of MyoD and Mef2 protein were not affected by Klf5 deletion (Figure 6—figure supplement 1), ChIP-seq revealed that MyoD binding was markedly decreased in Klf5 knockout cells compared to the GFP-targeted control cells on 3 day post-differentiation, as exemplified with Myod1, Myog, Myl4 and Mybph (Figure 6A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 6A and B.

claim: The decrease in MyoD binding after Klf5 deletion was similarly observed in another set of MyoD ChIP-seqs performed independently.
source: This decrease in MyoD binding after Klf5 deletion was similarly observed in another set of MyoD ChIP-seqs performed independently (Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by independent ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: Klf5 plays a significant role in the recruitment of MyoD to target genes.
source: These results suggest that Klf5 plays a significant role in the recruitment of MyoD to target genes.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the ChIP-seq and ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 6.

claim: In 4OH-Tmx treated Pax7CE/+;Klf5flox/flox satellite cells, Klf5 protein was undetectable.
source: In 4OH-Tmx treated Pax7CE/+;Klf5flox/floxSCs, Klf5 protein was undetectable.
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: In Klf5 knockout satellite cells, myogenin protein was markedly reduced as compared to that in control satellite cells.
source: In these Klf5 knockout cells, myogenin protein was markedly reduced as compared to that in control Pax7CE/+;Klf5flox/floxSCs without 4OH-Tmx treatment (Figure 7A).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: mRNA expression levels of Myog, Mybph and Myom2 were significantly decreased in Klf5 knockout satellite cells.
source: In addition, mRNA expression levels of Klf5 target genes exemplified by Myog, Mybph and Myom2 were significantly decreased in those cells (Figure 7B).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: Klf5 is indispensable for differentiation of primary satellite cells as well as C2C12 cells.
source: Collectively, these results indicate that Klf5 is indispensable for differentiation of primary SCs as well as C2C12 cells.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the satellite cell differentiation data shown in Figure 7.

claim: Klf5 is an essential mediator of skeletal muscle regeneration and myogenic differentiation.
source: We show that Klf5 is also an essential mediator of skeletal muscle regeneration and myogenic differentiation.
evidence: The claim is a summary statement supported by multiple lines of evidence presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: During muscle regeneration after cardiotoxin injection, Klf5 was induced in the nuclei of differentiating myoblasts and newly formed myofibers expressing myogenin in vivo.
